capture_method: Unauthenticated public web pages only; no provider API, account, credential, console, sales contact, reservation, purchase, SSH, endpoint, or GPU use.

sources.title: RTX 6000 Ada GPU Rental | Specs and Pricing
claims: RTX 6000 Ada is listed with 48 GB GDDR6 ECC.
Community Cloud is listed at $0.74/GPU-hour and Secure Cloud at $0.84/GPU-hour.
The page describes 31 regions and distinguishes community from secure capacity.

sources.title: GPU Cloud Pricing
claims: The RTX 6000 Ada Pod row lists 48 GB VRAM, 167 GB RAM, 10 vCPUs, and $0.84/hour.
Pods are described as dedicated GPU instances.

sources.title: RunPod concepts
claims: A Pod is a dedicated GPU or CPU instance for containerized AI/ML workloads.

sources.title: Zero GPU Pods on restart
claims: While a Pod is running, its assigned physical GPU is exclusively reserved for that user.
Stopping releases the physical GPU and restart availability is not guaranteed.

sources.title: Pods overview
claims: Secure Cloud operates in T3/T4 data centers; Community Cloud uses vetted peer-to-peer providers.
Pods accept custom containers from compatible registries and expose SSH or web-terminal access.
Docker Compose and nested Docker are not supported because RunPod runs the selected container.

sources.title: Manage Pod templates
claims: A custom Pod template can select a custom container image and start command for NVIDIA CUDA workloads.

sources.title: Billing overview
claims: Compute and local storage are billed per second with no data-transfer fee.
A new Pod requires a prepaid balance covering at least one hour.
Running container and volume disks cost $0.10/GB-month; network volumes under 1 TB cost $0.07/GB-month.

sources.title: Pod pricing
claims: On-demand Pods have no term and cannot be displaced by other users.
Savings plans are prepaid three- or six-month commitments, but the public documentation does not publish an RTX 6000 Ada plan rate.

sources.title: Global networking
claims: RunPod documents NVIDIA Pod locations in North America, Europe, Iceland, and Australia.
The public page does not bind RTX 6000 Ada stock to a particular current region.

sources.title: Full-stack AI cloud pricing
claims: One RTX 6000 Ada instance is listed with 48 GB VRAM, 10 CPUs, 60 GB RAM, $1.04/hour on-demand, and $0.364/hour spot.
One-year self-service reservation is 8% below on-demand and two-year reservation is 25% below on-demand.
NVMe and shared NVMe storage cost $0.20/GiB-month.

sources.title: Verda CLI instances
claims: Verda supports GPU VM creation with a location, OS image, SSH key, volumes, and an Ubuntu CUDA 13.0 open-docker image.
Public documentation directs users to an authenticated availability command for location-specific stock.

sources.title: Set up a CPU or GPU instance
claims: On-demand billing uses refundable prepaid ten-minute increments; spot may be evicted without warning.
Long-term rentals are paid up front.
The console exposes model/location availability, Ubuntu or Jupyter images, storage, SSH keys, and startup scripts.

sources.title: Locations and Sustainability
claims: Verda lists FIN-01, FIN-02, and FIN-03 in Helsinki, Finland.
The location page reports PUE values of 1.2, 1.3, and 1.2 but no RTX-specific sustained-clock or power-limit guarantee.

sources.title: QuantaCloud
claims: RTX 6000 Ada is listed at 48 GB, up to four per node, and $0.71/GPU-hour.
The listing says hourly billing with no commitment and that QuantaCloud may substitute equivalent or better hardware.
The public listing does not bind CPU, RAM, storage, network, region, exact device assignment, driver, or custom-container access.

sources.title: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation: Specs, AI Performance, and Cloud Pricing Guide
claims: The dated page reports $0.67/hour on-demand and $0.29/hour spot, bare-metal root SSH, per-minute billing, and no contract minimum.
The page explicitly warns that the May 2 prices may have changed.
Spheron's current catalog retrieved on July 28 does not list RTX 6000 Ada, so the dated rate is excluded from current venue hurdles.

sources.title: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation datasheet
claims: The card has 48 GB GDDR6 ECC, 960 GB/s bandwidth, PCIe Gen4 x16, 300 W total board power, and an active thermal solution.
The card has 18,176 CUDA cores and 568 fourth-generation Tensor Cores.

sources.title: NVIDIA Ada Lovelace Professional GPU Architecture
claims: RTX 6000 Ada uses AD102 with 142 enabled SMs and 98,304 KiB L2.
The architecture supports FP8, FP16, BF16, TF32, INT8, and INT4 Tensor Core formats.
Peak-format specifications are capability evidence only, not Gemma throughput evidence.

sources.title: NVIDIA Ada GPU Architecture Compatibility Guide for CUDA Applications
claims: Ada has compute capability 8.9.
CUDA Toolkit 11.8 is the first toolkit that can emit native sm_89 cubins.

sources.title: CUDA Math API: __nv_fp8_e5m2
claims: CUDA exposes the E5M2 FP8 datatype and device conversion operators.

sources.title: NVIDIA Container Toolkit: specialized configurations with Docker
claims: The NVIDIA runtime exposes selected GPUs and compute/utility driver capabilities to a CUDA container.
A CUDA image can enforce minimum CUDA/driver/architecture constraints; a host driver incompatible with the image prevents container startup.

sources.title: Existing campaign RunPod read-only snapshot
claims: The archived authenticated read showed zero Pods.
Its attempted GPU inventory path was invalid and established no RTX 6000 Ada availability.
It is not current stock evidence or authorization for this project.
